references.notes: Scite verify_papers 2026-11-15: verified, no editorial notices. The 2026-11-06 audit had recorded two errata (10.1002/acr.24401, 10.1002/acr.24566); not re-retrieved this run; errata are corrections, not retractions. claims.text: Dietary changes likely produce only small changes in serum urate; dietary factors may act as flare triggers

claims.text: ACR conditionally recommends limiting alcohol, purine intake and high-fructose corn syrup, and weight loss if overweight/obese
claims.quote: Using a weight loss program (no specific program endorsed) is conditionally recommended for those patients with gout who are overweight/obese, regardless of disease activity.

claims.text: Limiting purine intake is a conditional recommendation
claims.quote: Limiting purine intake is conditionally recommended for patients with gout, regardless of disease activity.

claims.text: Limiting high-fructose corn syrup is conditionally recommended

claims.text: Conditional recommendations reflect less than moderate or high certainty, including diet and lifestyle

claims.text: Cherry and dairy evidence low or very low certainty; no specific recommendation
claims.quote: The Voting Panel reviewed the data for cherries/cherry extract and dairy protein. The certainty of evidence drawn mainly from observational studies was low or very low, precluding specific recommendations on these topics.

claims.text: Vitamin C data insufficient to support its use

claims.text: HFCS associated with incident gout in Nurses Health Study; no data focused on patients with existing gout
claims.quote: In the Nurses’ Health Study, greater consumption of high-fructose corn syrup was associated with higher risk of incident gout (). However, there were no data focused on patients with existing gout.

claims.text: Obesity associated with incident gout; BMI decrease over 5 percent linked to 40 percent lower odds of recurrent flare

claims.text: One unit of beer raised serum urate by 0.16 mg/dL
